Thanks Alex — answers inline and a proposed mutual action plan below.

1) Pricing parity: In short, yes — Redwood will maintain the same net pricing on the Marketplace SKU for the first renewal period. Any marketplace fees are absorbed by Redwood for this transition; Ben includes a mapping table below.
2) Contract amendment vs PO: Procurement can either issue a Marketplace PO (preferred) or sign a short amendment that clarifies billing route. We typically accept a PO referencing the Marketplace subscription ID. If you need an amendment we can DocuSign a one-page amendment.
3) Data/SSO/support: No change to data residency or support SLAs; Marketplace billing only handles invoicing. Technical access and SSO remain under your existing setup.

Proposed mutual action plan (target cutover 2026-10-01):
- 8/27: Confirm PO vs Amendment decision (Luminar).
- 8/28–9/4: Redwood generates Marketplace SKUs and maps existing entitlements (Ben).
- 9/7–9/14: Procurement issues PO (or signs the amendment).
- 9/15–9/30: Azure listing activation + QA (Redwood & Azure co-ordination).
- 10/1: Marketplace subscription active for billing on renewal cycle.

Attachments: Luminar_MCP_Migration_Checklist.xlsx

Summary: we will create two Marketplace SKUs that correspond to your current seat and committed-throughput lines. Net pricing will be preserved for the first 12-month term. The differences to expect:
- Invoice cadence will be monthly through Azure (instead of our direct quarterly invoice).
- Invoice lines will reference Marketplace SKU IDs; we will provide a SKU mapping CSV for your AP team.
